Checked on the fake backend only (simulated R0). No hardware is attached, the package has no hardware backend and none was run, and the package is model-authored (deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017, run wC-021) and unreviewed (reviewed_by is null); no human review or hardware run is claimed. The upstream environment was never imported or run: nes-py is a native extension, the package requires CPython >=3.13 (pyproject.toml:10) and declares gymnasium and nes-py as dependencies (:38-41), so fake.py is a pure-Python stand-in and was never compared with an upstream run. The sim backend (GymnasiumDriver.open_native -> gymnasium.make('SuperMarioBros-v0')) is not listed in backends and was not run. NOT COVERED: the NES screen observation array. The real observation is nes-py's uint8 Box of shape 240 x 256 x 3 (robots/kautenja/nes-py/nes_py/_native.pyx:21-22,31 and nes_env.py:61-65 at nes-py commit 8d27b099f24a57afaac7339fab7ec0f1f96a59c8); the fake returns a 2 x 2 x 3 uint8 array of the same type and rank to keep receipts small, and the fidelity gaps name the real size. The fidelity contract is F0 with timestep_ms 0 because the pinned clone states no frame duration; one step is one NES frame and no dynamics are claimed. Warnings left as-is: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (it only sets the seed used by the next reset, so it makes no native call); G7.MAYBE_ABSENT x5 for action_space, observation_space, reset, step and close (they come from the external nes-py NESEnv base and each name occurs in the clone); G8.NO_UNIT x4 for the bridge-derived integer inputs ticks, action.index and seed twice (the family bridge supplies no units; declaring actions for reset and seed would expose undescribed reset inputs, as the exemplar explains). No operator-required Limit and no catalogue request were needed: the bounds are the environment's Discrete(256) action space (action.index 0..255) and the bridge's step/reset input schemas.
